question: Does BOLA-FINITE's finite-horizon buffer target improve the fixed BOLA score or safety-filtered highest-allowed rule on route-held-out Ghent LTE traces?

frozen_model.transfer_note: Candidate Transformer has no slot embeddings and supports variable candidate counts; the 8 kbps training-only startup rung is absent from this transfer ladder. Treat this as cross-route and changed-action-set diagnostic evidence.

measurement_limits: Only two route sessions are in the held-out split; report per trace and do not infer statistical significance.
The Ghent routes are historical observed HTTP goodput and not controlled link capacity or a modern cellular sample.
The dataset has segment sizes and metadata but no retained video media payload; visual quality is not measured.
Mean log-bitrate QoE is a bitrate proxy, not VMAF, MOS, or human acceptance.
The finite-video implementation adds the BOLA-FINITE dynamic buffer target and explicit wait. It omits request abandonment and dash.js player integration.
The frozen DQN trained with a seven-rung ladder that included an 8 kbps rung. The transfer ladder has six rungs, so the action set differs even though the model accepts variable candidate counts.
This is a frozen diagnostic comparison. No policy parameters are selected from the test outcomes.
